agent_evaluations.additional_notes: CRITICAL ERROR: Agent-item mismatch. This MCQ tests DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for major depressive disorder (moderate severity) vs other mood disorders. It does NOT test medication dosing, PBS compliance, Australian drug nomenclature, renal adjustments, or drug interactions - the core competencies of medication-management expert. While the explanation mentions 'SSRIs are first-line', the actual question stem is 'What is the most appropriate DIAGNOSIS?' not 'What is the most appropriate medication?'. Correct agent: mental-health-crisis-expert or psychiatry specialist.

strengths: Comprehensive coverage of depression, anxiety, bipolar, psychosis, and suicide risk topics
Correct Australian medication names (sertraline, escitalopram, olanzapine, quetiapine)
Mental Health Act involuntary criteria correctly outlined (4 criteria: mentally ill, risk, treatment needed, no alternative)
Appropriate emphasis on benzodiazepines + thiamine for alcohol withdrawal
Clozapine monitoring schedule correctly specified (weekly FBC 18wk → fortnightly → monthly)
First-episode psychosis management appropriate (URGENT EPIS referral + low-dose antipsychotic)
Metabolic risk hierarchy correct (Aripiprazole < Risperidone < Quetiapine < Olanzapine/Clozapine)
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome recognized as medical emergency (rigidity + fever + autonomic instability)

detailed_feedback.safe_t_assessment: SAFE-T framework mentioned in agent instructions but not systematically applied across MCQs. Only PSY-SUICIDE-MHA subtopic addresses suicide risk assessment thoroughly. Depression and psychosis MCQs should integrate SAFE-T assessment as this is zero-tolerance criterion.
detailed_feedback.mental_health_act: Mental Health Act criteria correctly outlined in theory but state-specific differences (NSW/VIC/QLD) not clearly distinguished in practice questions. Need more emphasis on 'least restrictive alternative' principle and Community Treatment Orders.
detailed_feedback.medication_safety: Strong medication safety content - correct Australian names, appropriate dosing, monitoring requirements. Minor gap: refeeding syndrome phosphate monitoring could be more explicit.
detailed_feedback.cultural_safety: MAJOR GAP - No Aboriginal/TSI mental health considerations in any MCQ. This is critical omission given 10% AHPRA weighting for cultural safety. Need MCQs addressing: Aboriginal liaison, SEWB framework, historical trauma, culturally appropriate communication.

critical_gaps: Zero MCQs address Aboriginal/TSI mental health presentations or cultural safety
SAFE-T framework not systematically applied to depression/psychosis MCQs with suicide risk
Protective factors assessment underrepresented (only 1 MCQ: PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-731)
No MCQs on Mental Health Act tribunal review process or patient rights
No MCQs on capacity assessment in psychiatric context (only 1: PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-300)
No MCQs on crisis de-escalation techniques (verbal de-escalation, environmental modification)
recommendations_for_improvement: Add 10-15 MCQs on Aboriginal/TSI mental health (cultural safety, SEWB, historical trauma, Aboriginal liaison)
Integrate SAFE-T assessment into ALL suicide risk MCQs (currently only in dedicated suicide topic)
Add MCQs distinguishing NSW/VIC/QLD Mental Health Act procedures
Include more MCQs on protective factors and safety planning (beyond crisis contacts)
Add capacity assessment MCQs (understanding, appreciation, reasoning, choice)
Include de-escalation techniques MCQs (verbal, environmental, least restrictive interventions)
